ticket.title: common minted under storypole prefix, and legacy GB- keys collide with the harness
ticket.description:
MEASURED 2026-11-08, while fixing GB-345's second half. `storypole ledger-reconcile` fails with
`UNIQUE constraint failed: tasks.ticket_key_lower`. The data is not at fault: across 355 distinct keys there are no
duplicates inside any one repository, and the collisions that exist are the legitimate kind:

  gb-342 -> common, .        gb-343 -> common, .
  gb-344 -> storypole, .     gb-345 -> storypole, .

Four keys owned by two repositories each. Under ADR 0007 and ADR 0010 a ticket key is scoped to its repository, so two
repositories owning GB-342 is correct by construction - and the unified index cannot hold both, because it constrains
ticket_key_lower to be unique across the whole suite.

I CAUSED HALF THE COLLISIONS, which is the part worth recording. GB-342, GB-343, GB-344 and GB-345 were all minted into
the ROOT store today by me, using `storypole defer` at the suite root, without noticing that per-repository numbering had
landed and that common and storypole had already used those numbers. Nothing warned: the root store mints from its own
sequence and had no reason to look at its members. So the tool behaved as designed and the design is the problem.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FAILING VERB: the unified index is what the workspace rollup and the panel read. If it cannot
represent a legal pair of tickets, then either the rollup has been silently dropping one of each colliding pair (worse
than failing loudly) or this is the first time anyone tried. Either way, "one key names one ticket" is currently false at
the suite level while being true at the repository level, and every surface has to pick which it believes.

THREE RESOLUTIONS, none chosen:
  (a) index identity becomes (repo, key) and everything that renders a key names its repository - the only option that
      keeps ADR 0007 intact; it is also the option SP-38 asked for independently, since a cross-repository edge target
      already has to render as `KEY (repo)`;
  (b) the ROOT store stops minting keys that a member owns, i.e. allocation becomes suite-wide - simple, but it makes
      the root privileged and its numbering unknowable without reading eleven stores;
  (c) the root mints under a distinct prefix (GBR- vs GB-) - cheap, immediately unambiguous, and it quietly says a root
      ticket is a different sort of thing.

(a) matches the direction the suite already chose. It is also the most work, which is the honest trade.

DECIDED BY THE ARCHITECT 2026-11-08, and it reframes the ticket: this was never an index design problem.

THE MODEL:
  * `GB-*` is the HARNESS. It is for harness-level and multi-repository work only.
  * Every repository mints under its own configured prefix - BA, BW, CH, CO, DA, JN, MTR, OF, RB, SH, SP.
  * A ticket that turns out to be single-repository may be REMINTED into that repository's prefix.
  * A ticket that is multi-repository or harness-level STAYS `GB-*`, and is LINKED to the per-repository tickets that
    carry the actual work: GB-NN -> SP-NN & OF-NN.

So two repositories owning `GB-342` was never legal-and-unrepresentable. It was a configuration fault: one repository was
minting keys it had no business minting. The index constraint is right, and "one key names one ticket" holds suite-wide.

ROOT CAUSE, verified: `common/.gaugeblock/storypole/config.toml` declared `ticket_prefix = "SP"` - storypole's prefix, in
the wrong repository - so `common` minted `SP-*` keys, and its eleven legacy `GB-*` keys came from the pre-migration
ledger before prefixes existed. Two other repositories' prefixes appeared in one store.

FIXED: common's prefix is now `CO`, verified by minting a probe ticket (`CO-1`) and deleting it again.

OWED, and it is a migration rather than an edit:
  1. common holds 11 legacy `GB-*` keys, which collide with harness numbering. Each is single-repository work by
     definition, so each should be reminted `CO-NN` per the model above, keeping its uuid and its history.
  2. common also holds CO-1, CO-2 and CO-3 - keys minted under storypole's prefix before this fix. Same treatment.
  3. storypole's own store holds legacy `GB-*` keys (SP-38 among them) that belong in `SP-*` once reminting is
     possible.
  4. Reminting needs the links written at the same time, or a reminted ticket loses the harness ticket that spawned it.
     That is the GB-NN -> SP-NN relationship, and it is the same cross-ledger edge SP-38 is about, so the two should be
     done together rather than twice.

Until that migration runs, `ledger-reconcile` cannot open the unified index and the workspace rollup cannot hold a
colliding pair. The diagnostic that names collisions instead of dying on a constraint is the right interim state.

DIAGNOSTIC LIVE 2026-11-08 (83bf3b3). `ledger-reconcile` now names the collisions instead of dying on a raw constraint,
and reports the state accurately:

  GB-342: ., common      GB-345: ., storypole
  GB-343: ., common      GB-346: ., storypole
  GB-344: ., storypole   GB-347: ., storypole

That is the interim state this ticket wanted: the failure is legible and points at GB-346 and GB-347, so whoever meets it
learns the cause in one run rather than in an afternoon.

The first run of the diagnostic printed every repository as `/`, because the discovered paths are absolute and I took the
first component of the path instead of the first component relative to the root. Caught by reading the output, not by
checking the exit code - which is now the fourth time this session that reading beat testing.

RE-CHECKED 2026-11-12: ledger-reconcile runs without the cross-repository key collision it was filed for and reports index and ledger agree, keyed 387 records.
